info.name: Creators' Vault API
info.description:
Backend for Creators’ Vault — an intelligent digital asset management workspace.

All routes are versioned under `/api/v1`.

**Auth:** obtain a JWT by completing the Google OAuth flow at
`GET /api/v1/auth/google`, then send it as `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`.

**Stubbed modules:** marketplace and payments expose their final request and
response shapes but do not process real transactions.

item.name: Upload one or more files, or a folder as a zip.

request.description: Send files under the `files` field. One asset is created per file. Pass `expandZip=true` to unpack a .zip into one asset per entry — that is how a folder is imported. Returns an array even for a single file.

item.name: Import an asset from a pasted URL.

request.description: Fetches the page for its title, description and preview image unless `fetchMetadata` is false. A site that is slow or blocks scrapers does not fail the import — the domain is used as the title instead.

item.name: Import a purchased asset from a marketplace link.

request.description: The URL import plus manually entered purchase details. No marketplace API is contacted — every purchase field is optional and supplied by you.
Only the fields you send change. Sending `tags` replaces the whole tag set for the asset.

item.name: Move an asset to the trash.

request.description: A soft delete — assets are never hard-deleted. The file stays in storage and the asset stops counting against your quota. Reversible with POST /assets/:id/restore.

item.name: Restore an asset from the trash.

item.name: Exchange a refresh token for a new token pair.

request.description: Refresh tokens rotate: the presented token is revoked and a new one returned. Replaying an already-rotated token revokes every session for that user.
Idempotent — revoking an unknown or already-revoked token is not an error.

item.name: Revoke every refresh token for the authenticated user.
extension
item.description: Browser-extension tokens and the capture endpoint

request.description: Call this from the signed-in web app and paste the result into the extension. The token is returned ONCE and only its hash is stored — it cannot be shown again.

item.name: List the authenticated user’s extension tokens.

request.description: Shows a prefix and last-used time, never the token itself.
Takes effect immediately. The record is kept, marked revoked, so the user can still see it in the list.

item.name: Verify an extension token and identify its owner.

request.description: The extension calls this once at setup to confirm the pasted token works.

item.name: Capture the current page as an asset.

request.description: Authenticated by the extension token, not a JWT. Runs the same asset-creation path as POST /assets/from-url — same validation, tag creation, project checks and background indexing — and records sourceType "extension".

item.name: Change a relationship’s type or reason.

request.description: Re-pointing an edge is not an update — delete it and create the new one.
Permanent, and neither asset is affected — an edge holds no content of its own.

item.name: search
item.description: Keyword search, semantic search and similarity

query.description: The search text. Matches title, description, category, tags and platform.
Keyword matching produces no usable relevance rank, so results are ordered by a real column. Use POST /search/semantic when relevance ordering is what you want.
Tag slugs. An asset must carry them all.

request.description: Matches title, description, category, source platform and tag names. Makes no AI call, so it is instant and free — use this for most queries.
Embeds the query and ranks assets by cosine similarity to their stored vectors. Degrades to keyword search rather than failing — always check `strategy` in the response.

item.name: Whether semantic search is usable right now, and how much is indexed.
Index the authenticated user’s assets that have no embedding yet.

request.description: Indexing normally happens automatically in the background when an asset is created. This catches up assets created while the provider was down, or before one was configured, and is the migration path after changing EMBEDDING_DRIVER.

item.name: Assets similar to this one, with a similarity score.

request.description: Compares stored embeddings, so it makes no AI call. Returns an empty list with a `reason` when the asset has not been indexed yet.
Idempotent — a name that slugs to an existing tag returns that tag rather than a conflict. Tags are also created implicitly when you send `tags` on an asset.

query.description: Free-text filter. The fields it covers are documented per endpoint.
`usageCount` sorts by how many live assets carry the tag.
Hide tags that are not on any live asset.

request.description: Sorted by usage by default. `q` matches both the name and the slug.

item.name: Suggest tags for an asset or for typed text.

request.description: Blends three signals: tags you already use that match the text, tags that co-occur on your similar assets, and salient new terms. Works with no AI provider configured; when one is, an extra semantic pass re-ranks the results.
Renaming also changes the slug, which is what asset filters use — update any saved filters accordingly.
Permanent, unlike assets and projects — a tag holds no content, so deleting it only detaches it from assets. No asset is deleted.
